dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Post-infectious (parainfectious) brainstem–cerebellar disorder presenting as ocular flutter, most likely a self-limited immune-mediated inflammatory process affecting omnipause neurons and/or the fastigial nucleus following recent viral upper respiratory tract infection.

1. Paraneoplastic opsoclonus/flutter syndrome (occult neuroblastoma in adults, e.g., anti-Ri/ANNA-2 or anti-Hu associated small-cell lung or breast carcinoma)
2. Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis or atypical Miller Fisher syndrome (post-infectious anti-GQ1b spectrum disorder)
3. Multiple sclerosis / clinically isolated syndrome involving the dorsal pons or cerebellar vermis (despite current normal MRI, worth follow-up imaging in 3–6 months)
